description: Calls through the Python client (decide, bound functions, interface shorthands, escalation, dispatch and graphs) over a scripted engine. 'questions' is what each llm or human step was shown. 'expect' is the result or the error. The timing.ms of a decision an llm or human step made is written '<elapsed>'.

question.instructions: Given the agent's goal, its plan and the latest tool result, what should the agent do next? continue: the latest call worked and steps of the plan remain, or it returned only part of a list and the goal needs the rest (fetch the next part). retry: the call failed for a temporary reason (a timeout, the service unavailable, a rate limit with a short wait) and the attempts so far are fewer than the retry limit; make the same call again. change_approach: the call cannot succeed as it was made because of the agent's own mistake (a value in the wrong format or not allowed, an id or name that differs from the one in the goal, a search spelled differently from the goal); correct the call or use another tool. stop: report back to the user: the goal is now done (the last step of the plan worked, or the result itself answers the goal), or it cannot be done (the record in the goal does not exist, or the request was refused for a reason no retry or other tool can change). escalate: a person must act: permission denied, login expired, approval needed, or a temporary failure has already used every allowed retry.

criteria.change_approach: Change approach: the call cannot work as it was made (a wrong value, a typo, a bad format); fix the call or use another tool.
criteria.continue: Continue: the step worked (or returned part of a list with more to fetch); go on to the next step.
criteria.escalate: Escalate: a person has to act: permission denied, login expired, approval needed, or a temporary failure has used up every allowed retry.
criteria.retry: Retry: a temporary failure, and attempts so far are below the retry limit; make the same call again.
criteria.stop: Stop: report back to the user: the goal is done, or it cannot be done and nothing the agent can do will change that.

question.instructions: A bank checks each customer, or each party named in a payment, against one entry from a sanctions list or another watch list. Is the customer the party on the list? Names agree when the customer's name is the listed name or one of its aliases, allowing for other spellings or transliterations, a different order of the names, initials, a missing middle name and small typing mistakes. The deciding detail is the date of birth for a person, the country of registration for a company or organisation, and the IMO number for a ship. A year of birth alone cannot confirm a person, but a different year rules them out. A different kind of party, such as a ship instead of a person, is never the listed party. Nationality, occupation and the other details do not decide.

criteria.match: Match: the customer is the listed party. The names agree and the deciding detail agrees with the entry.
criteria.possible_match: Possible match: the names agree and nothing contradicts the entry, but the deciding detail is missing from the customer record or from the entry, so a person must check it.
criteria.no_match: No match: the customer is a different party. The names clearly differ, the customer is a different kind of party, or the deciding detail contradicts the entry.

question.instructions: Which type of clause is this contract provision? Choose the clause type that best matches the main topic of the provision.

criteria.adjustments: Adjustments: how amounts, prices, share numbers or other terms are adjusted when stated events happen (for example a stock split).
criteria.agreements: Agreements: a provision headed 'Agreements', stating what the parties agree to or which other agreements apply.
criteria.amendments: Amendments: how the contract can be amended, usually only in writing signed by the parties.
criteria.anti_corruption_laws: Anti-corruption laws: promises to comply with bribery and corruption laws such as the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.
criteria.applicable_laws: Applicable laws: which laws apply to the contract or to the parties' conduct, or a promise to follow applicable laws.
criteria.approvals: Approvals: approvals that are needed or have been obtained (from boards, shareholders, regulators or the other party).
criteria.arbitration: Arbitration: disputes are settled by arbitration, with the rules, place and procedure for it.
criteria.assignments: Assignments: whether and how a party may transfer its rights or duties under the contract to someone else.
criteria.assigns: Assigns: the contract binds and benefits the parties' permitted assigns (those to whom rights are transferred).
criteria.authority: Authority: a party states it has the power and authority to enter into and perform the contract.
criteria.authorizations: Authorizations: the contract has been duly authorized by the necessary corporate action, or needed permits are held.
criteria.base_salary: Base salary: the employee's fixed yearly pay and how it is paid or reviewed.
criteria.benefits: Benefits: employee benefits such as health insurance, retirement plans and other benefit programs.
criteria.binding_effects: Binding effect: the contract is binding on, and benefits, the parties and their successors.
criteria.books: Books: keeping accurate books of account and records, and access to inspect them.
criteria.brokers: Brokers: no broker or finder is owed a fee for the deal, or who pays any such fee.
criteria.capitalization: Capitalization: the company's authorized and issued shares and other equity.
criteria.change_in_control: Change in control: what happens when ownership or control of a party changes (for example a merger or sale).
criteria.closings: Closings: when and where the deal closes and what is delivered at closing.
criteria.compliance_with_laws: Compliance with laws: a party complies, or will comply, with all laws that apply to it.
criteria.confidentiality: Confidentiality: keeping information secret and limits on using or disclosing it.
criteria.consent_to_jurisdiction: Consent to jurisdiction: the parties consent to the jurisdiction of named courts for disputes.
criteria.consents: Consents: consents of third parties or authorities that are needed or have been obtained, or how consent may be given.
criteria.construction: Construction: rules for reading and interpreting the contract (for example no presumption against the drafter).
criteria.cooperation: Cooperation: the parties will cooperate and assist each other to carry out the contract.
criteria.costs: Costs: who bears costs and expenses, such as legal costs or costs of enforcement.
criteria.counterparts: Counterparts: the contract may be signed in separate copies, including electronic signatures, which together form one agreement.
criteria.death: Death: what happens under the contract if the employee or a party dies.
criteria.defined_terms: Defined terms: states that capitalized terms have the meanings defined elsewhere, or lists defined terms.
criteria.definitions: Definitions: a list of terms and the meanings they have in the contract.
criteria.disability: Disability: what happens if the employee becomes disabled and unable to work, and how disability is defined.
criteria.disclosures: Disclosures: information that has been or must be disclosed, or statements that disclosures are accurate and complete.
criteria.duties: Duties: the duties and responsibilities of a person's role (for example an employee's or officer's duties).
criteria.effective_dates: Effective date: the date on which the contract or a provision takes effect.
criteria.effectiveness: Effectiveness: when and under what conditions the contract becomes effective.
criteria.employment: Employment: the employment relationship itself, such as the position, start and at-will terms.
criteria.enforceability: Enforceability: the contract is valid, binding and enforceable against the party, subject to usual exceptions.
criteria.enforcements: Enforcement: how the contract's rights and obligations can be enforced.
criteria.entire_agreements: Entire agreement: the contract is the whole agreement and replaces all earlier agreements on the subject.
criteria.erisa: ERISA: matters under the U.S. Employee Retirement Income Security Act, such as pension and benefit plan compliance.
criteria.existence: Existence: a party is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, and will keep its existence.
criteria.expenses: Expenses: which party pays or reimburses which expenses.
criteria.fees: Fees: fees payable under the contract (for example commitment, agency or service fees).
criteria.financial_statements: Financial statements: the accuracy of financial statements, or the duty to deliver them.
criteria.forfeitures: Forfeiture: when awards, shares or rights are forfeited (lost), for example on leaving employment.
criteria.further_assurances: Further assurances: the parties will sign further documents and take further steps needed to carry out the contract.
criteria.general: General: a provision headed 'General' that holds assorted general terms.
criteria.governing_laws: Governing law: which state's or country's law governs the contract.
criteria.headings: Headings: section headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning.
criteria.indemnifications: Indemnification: one party must compensate and defend the other against losses and claims.
criteria.indemnity: Indemnity: a promise to hold another party harmless from losses, claims and liabilities.
criteria.insurances: Insurance: insurance a party must carry, or the insurance it has in place.
criteria.integration: Integration: the written contract fully integrates the parties' agreement and supersedes earlier understandings.
criteria.intellectual_property: Intellectual property: ownership, use or protection of patents, trademarks, copyrights and other intellectual property.
criteria.interests: Interests: interest on amounts owed, such as interest rates and how interest is calculated, or ownership interests.
criteria.interpretations: Interpretation: rules for interpreting words in the contract (for example 'including' means 'including without limitation').
criteria.jurisdictions: Jurisdiction: which courts have jurisdiction over disputes under the contract.
criteria.liens: Liens: limits on creating liens or security interests on assets, or statements that assets are free of liens.
criteria.litigations: Litigation: there are no pending or threatened lawsuits or proceedings, or how litigation is handled.
criteria.miscellaneous: Miscellaneous: a provision headed 'Miscellaneous' that gathers assorted final terms.
criteria.modifications: Modifications: how the contract can be changed or modified, usually only in writing.
criteria.no_conflicts: No conflicts: entering into the contract does not breach the party's charter, other contracts or the law.
criteria.no_defaults: No defaults: no default or event of default has happened or is continuing.
criteria.no_waivers: No waiver: failing or delaying to use a right does not waive that right.
criteria.non_disparagement: Non-disparagement: a party will not make negative or damaging statements about the other.
criteria.notices: Notices: how formal notices must be given, and to which addresses.
criteria.organizations: Organization: a party is duly organized and in good standing under the laws of its home jurisdiction.
criteria.participations: Participations: a lender may sell participations (shares) in its loans to other parties.
criteria.payments: Payments: how, when and where payments must be made.
criteria.positions: Position: the job title and position the employee holds.
criteria.powers: Powers: the powers of a party, agent or trustee, or a party's corporate power to act.
criteria.publicity: Publicity: limits on press releases and public announcements about the contract.
criteria.qualifications: Qualification: a party is qualified to do business in the jurisdictions where it operates.
criteria.records: Records: keeping records and giving access to them.
criteria.releases: Release: a party gives up (releases) claims it has against the other.
criteria.remedies: Remedies: the remedies available for a breach, and whether they are cumulative.
criteria.representations: Representations: statements of fact a party makes to the other, or how long such statements survive.
criteria.sales: Sales: the sale of goods, shares or assets, or limits on selling them.
criteria.sanctions: Sanctions: compliance with economic sanctions laws and dealings with sanctioned persons or countries.
criteria.severability: Severability: if one provision is invalid, the rest of the contract remains in force.
criteria.solvency: Solvency: a party is solvent, able to pay its debts, and will not become insolvent because of the deal.
criteria.specific_performance: Specific performance: a party may ask a court to order the other to perform, not just pay damages.
criteria.submission_to_jurisdiction: Submission to jurisdiction: the parties submit to the jurisdiction of named courts.
criteria.subsidiaries: Subsidiaries: the party's subsidiaries, their ownership, or duties that extend to them.
criteria.successors: Successors: the contract binds and benefits the parties' successors.
criteria.survival: Survival: which provisions continue to apply after the contract ends.
criteria.tax_withholdings: Tax withholding: amounts may be withheld from payments to cover required taxes.
criteria.taxes: Taxes: who pays which taxes, tax treatment, and tax gross-ups.
criteria.terminations: Termination: how and when the contract or employment can be ended, and what follows.
criteria.terms: Term: how long the contract or employment lasts, and renewal.
criteria.titles: Title: ownership of property or assets, and when title passes; or a person's job title.
criteria.transactions_with_affiliates: Transactions with affiliates: limits on deals with affiliated companies, which must be on fair terms.
criteria.use_of_proceeds: Use of proceeds: what the money raised or borrowed may be used for.
criteria.vacations: Vacation: the employee's paid vacation or time off.
criteria.venues: Venue: where (in which place or court) lawsuits must be brought.
criteria.vesting: Vesting: when options, shares or benefits vest (become the holder's own), and the schedule.
criteria.waiver_of_jury_trials: Waiver of jury trial: the parties give up the right to a jury trial in disputes.
criteria.waivers: Waiver: how rights under the contract can be waived, usually only in writing.
criteria.warranties: Warranties: promises that stated facts are true or that goods or services meet stated standards.
criteria.withholdings: Withholding: payments are subject to withholding of required taxes and other deductions.

criteria.indemnity: Indemnity: a promise to hold another party harmless from losses, claims and liabilities.
criteria.insurances: Insurance: insurance a party must carry, or the insurance it has in place.
criteria.integration: Integration: the written contract fully integrates the parties' agreement and supersedes earlier understandings.
criteria.intellectual_property: Intellectual property: ownership, use or protection of patents, trademarks, copyrights and other intellectual property.
criteria.interests: Interests: interest on amounts owed, such as interest rates and how interest is calculated, or ownership interests.
criteria.interpretations: Interpretation: rules for interpreting words in the contract (for example 'including' means 'including without limitation').
criteria.jurisdictions: Jurisdiction: which courts have jurisdiction over disputes under the contract.
criteria.liens: Liens: limits on creating liens or security interests on assets, or statements that assets are free of liens.
criteria.litigations: Litigation: there are no pending or threatened lawsuits or proceedings, or how litigation is handled.
criteria.miscellaneous: Miscellaneous: a provision headed 'Miscellaneous' that gathers assorted final terms.
criteria.modifications: Modifications: how the contract can be changed or modified, usually only in writing.
criteria.no_conflicts: No conflicts: entering into the contract does not breach the party's charter, other contracts or the law.
criteria.no_defaults: No defaults: no default or event of default has happened or is continuing.
criteria.no_waivers: No waiver: failing or delaying to use a right does not waive that right.
criteria.non_disparagement: Non-disparagement: a party will not make negative or damaging statements about the other.
criteria.notices: Notices: how formal notices must be given, and to which addresses.
criteria.organizations: Organization: a party is duly organized and in good standing under the laws of its home jurisdiction.
criteria.participations: Participations: a lender may sell participations (shares) in its loans to other parties.
criteria.payments: Payments: how, when and where payments must be made.
criteria.positions: Position: the job title and position the employee holds.
criteria.powers: Powers: the powers of a party, agent or trustee, or a party's corporate power to act.
criteria.publicity: Publicity: limits on press releases and public announcements about the contract.
criteria.qualifications: Qualification: a party is qualified to do business in the jurisdictions where it operates.
criteria.records: Records: keeping records and giving access to them.
criteria.releases: Release: a party gives up (releases) claims it has against the other.
criteria.remedies: Remedies: the remedies available for a breach, and whether they are cumulative.
criteria.representations: Representations: statements of fact a party makes to the other, or how long such statements survive.
criteria.sales: Sales: the sale of goods, shares or assets, or limits on selling them.
criteria.sanctions: Sanctions: compliance with economic sanctions laws and dealings with sanctioned persons or countries.
criteria.severability: Severability: if one provision is invalid, the rest of the contract remains in force.
criteria.solvency: Solvency: a party is solvent, able to pay its debts, and will not become insolvent because of the deal.
criteria.specific_performance: Specific performance: a party may ask a court to order the other to perform, not just pay damages.
criteria.submission_to_jurisdiction: Submission to jurisdiction: the parties submit to the jurisdiction of named courts.
criteria.subsidiaries: Subsidiaries: the party's subsidiaries, their ownership, or duties that extend to them.
criteria.successors: Successors: the contract binds and benefits the parties' successors.
criteria.survival: Survival: which provisions continue to apply after the contract ends.
criteria.tax_withholdings: Tax withholding: amounts may be withheld from payments to cover required taxes.
criteria.taxes: Taxes: who pays which taxes, tax treatment, and tax gross-ups.
criteria.terminations: Termination: how and when the contract or employment can be ended, and what follows.
criteria.terms: Term: how long the contract or employment lasts, and renewal.
criteria.titles: Title: ownership of property or assets, and when title passes; or a person's job title.
criteria.transactions_with_affiliates: Transactions with affiliates: limits on deals with affiliated companies, which must be on fair terms.
criteria.use_of_proceeds: Use of proceeds: what the money raised or borrowed may be used for.
criteria.vacations: Vacation: the employee's paid vacation or time off.
criteria.venues: Venue: where (in which place or court) lawsuits must be brought.
criteria.vesting: Vesting: when options, shares or benefits vest (become the holder's own), and the schedule.
criteria.waiver_of_jury_trials: Waiver of jury trial: the parties give up the right to a jury trial in disputes.
criteria.waivers: Waiver: how rights under the contract can be waived, usually only in writing.
criteria.warranties: Warranties: promises that stated facts are true or that goods or services meet stated standards.
criteria.withholdings: Withholding: payments are subject to withholding of required taxes and other deductions.

criteria.consents: Consents: consents of third parties or authorities that are needed or have been obtained, or how consent may be given.
criteria.construction: Construction: rules for reading and interpreting the contract (for example no presumption against the drafter).
criteria.cooperation: Cooperation: the parties will cooperate and assist each other to carry out the contract.
criteria.costs: Costs: who bears costs and expenses, such as legal costs or costs of enforcement.
criteria.counterparts: Counterparts: the contract may be signed in separate copies, including electronic signatures, which together form one agreement.
criteria.death: Death: what happens under the contract if the employee or a party dies.
criteria.defined_terms: Defined terms: states that capitalized terms have the meanings defined elsewhere, or lists defined terms.
criteria.definitions: Definitions: a list of terms and the meanings they have in the contract.
criteria.disability: Disability: what happens if the employee becomes disabled and unable to work, and how disability is defined.
criteria.disclosures: Disclosures: information that has been or must be disclosed, or statements that disclosures are accurate and complete.
criteria.duties: Duties: the duties and responsibilities of a person's role (for example an employee's or officer's duties).
criteria.effective_dates: Effective date: the date on which the contract or a provision takes effect.
criteria.effectiveness: Effectiveness: when and under what conditions the contract becomes effective.
criteria.employment: Employment: the employment relationship itself, such as the position, start and at-will terms.
criteria.enforceability: Enforceability: the contract is valid, binding and enforceable against the party, subject to usual exceptions.
criteria.enforcements: Enforcement: how the contract's rights and obligations can be enforced.
criteria.entire_agreements: Entire agreement: the contract is the whole agreement and replaces all earlier agreements on the subject.
criteria.erisa: ERISA: matters under the U.S. Employee Retirement Income Security Act, such as pension and benefit plan compliance.
criteria.existence: Existence: a party is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, and will keep its existence.
criteria.expenses: Expenses: which party pays or reimburses which expenses.
criteria.fees: Fees: fees payable under the contract (for example commitment, agency or service fees).
criteria.financial_statements: Financial statements: the accuracy of financial statements, or the duty to deliver them.
criteria.forfeitures: Forfeiture: when awards, shares or rights are forfeited (lost), for example on leaving employment.
criteria.further_assurances: Further assurances: the parties will sign further documents and take further steps needed to carry out the contract.
criteria.general: General: a provision headed 'General' that holds assorted general terms.
criteria.governing_laws: Governing law: which state's or country's law governs the contract.
criteria.headings: Headings: section headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning.
criteria.indemnifications: Indemnification: one party must compensate and defend the other against losses and claims.
criteria.indemnity: Indemnity: a promise to hold another party harmless from losses, claims and liabilities.
criteria.insurances: Insurance: insurance a party must carry, or the insurance it has in place.
criteria.integration: Integration: the written contract fully integrates the parties' agreement and supersedes earlier understandings.
criteria.intellectual_property: Intellectual property: ownership, use or protection of patents, trademarks, copyrights and other intellectual property.
criteria.interests: Interests: interest on amounts owed, such as interest rates and how interest is calculated, or ownership interests.
criteria.interpretations: Interpretation: rules for interpreting words in the contract (for example 'including' means 'including without limitation').
criteria.jurisdictions: Jurisdiction: which courts have jurisdiction over disputes under the contract.
criteria.liens: Liens: limits on creating liens or security interests on assets, or statements that assets are free of liens.
criteria.litigations: Litigation: there are no pending or threatened lawsuits or proceedings, or how litigation is handled.
criteria.miscellaneous: Miscellaneous: a provision headed 'Miscellaneous' that gathers assorted final terms.
criteria.modifications: Modifications: how the contract can be changed or modified, usually only in writing.
criteria.no_conflicts: No conflicts: entering into the contract does not breach the party's charter, other contracts or the law.
criteria.no_defaults: No defaults: no default or event of default has happened or is continuing.
criteria.no_waivers: No waiver: failing or delaying to use a right does not waive that right.
criteria.non_disparagement: Non-disparagement: a party will not make negative or damaging statements about the other.
criteria.notices: Notices: how formal notices must be given, and to which addresses.
criteria.organizations: Organization: a party is duly organized and in good standing under the laws of its home jurisdiction.
criteria.participations: Participations: a lender may sell participations (shares) in its loans to other parties.
criteria.payments: Payments: how, when and where payments must be made.
criteria.positions: Position: the job title and position the employee holds.
criteria.powers: Powers: the powers of a party, agent or trustee, or a party's corporate power to act.
criteria.publicity: Publicity: limits on press releases and public announcements about the contract.
criteria.qualifications: Qualification: a party is qualified to do business in the jurisdictions where it operates.
criteria.records: Records: keeping records and giving access to them.
criteria.releases: Release: a party gives up (releases) claims it has against the other.
criteria.remedies: Remedies: the remedies available for a breach, and whether they are cumulative.
criteria.representations: Representations: statements of fact a party makes to the other, or how long such statements survive.
criteria.sales: Sales: the sale of goods, shares or assets, or limits on selling them.
criteria.sanctions: Sanctions: compliance with economic sanctions laws and dealings with sanctioned persons or countries.
criteria.severability: Severability: if one provision is invalid, the rest of the contract remains in force.
criteria.solvency: Solvency: a party is solvent, able to pay its debts, and will not become insolvent because of the deal.
criteria.specific_performance: Specific performance: a party may ask a court to order the other to perform, not just pay damages.
criteria.submission_to_jurisdiction: Submission to jurisdiction: the parties submit to the jurisdiction of named courts.
criteria.subsidiaries: Subsidiaries: the party's subsidiaries, their ownership, or duties that extend to them.
criteria.successors: Successors: the contract binds and benefits the parties' successors.
criteria.survival: Survival: which provisions continue to apply after the contract ends.
criteria.tax_withholdings: Tax withholding: amounts may be withheld from payments to cover required taxes.
criteria.taxes: Taxes: who pays which taxes, tax treatment, and tax gross-ups.
criteria.terminations: Termination: how and when the contract or employment can be ended, and what follows.
criteria.terms: Term: how long the contract or employment lasts, and renewal.
criteria.titles: Title: ownership of property or assets, and when title passes; or a person's job title.
criteria.transactions_with_affiliates: Transactions with affiliates: limits on deals with affiliated companies, which must be on fair terms.
criteria.use_of_proceeds: Use of proceeds: what the money raised or borrowed may be used for.
criteria.vacations: Vacation: the employee's paid vacation or time off.
criteria.venues: Venue: where (in which place or court) lawsuits must be brought.
criteria.vesting: Vesting: when options, shares or benefits vest (become the holder's own), and the schedule.
criteria.waiver_of_jury_trials: Waiver of jury trial: the parties give up the right to a jury trial in disputes.
criteria.waivers: Waiver: how rights under the contract can be waived, usually only in writing.
criteria.warranties: Warranties: promises that stated facts are true or that goods or services meet stated standards.
criteria.withholdings: Withholding: payments are subject to withholding of required taxes and other deductions.
